name: Turkish Cypriot Molohiya
description: Molohiya, a real jute-leaf stew genuinely distinct from the shared Greek-Cypriot dishes, is especially prominent in Turkish Cypriot culture, traditionally made from dried, rehydrated leaves - real technique washes and soaks the leaves to rehydrate before a real long simmer of an hour or more with lemon and warming spices; real jute leaves aren't a distinct item here, so okra and spinach stand in together for a similar mucilaginous texture.

ingredients_full.note: sliced, standing in for jute leaf's texture

ingredients.note: sliced, standing in for jute leaf's texture

steps_detailed: Brown the chicken with the onion and garlic, 8-9 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 15 minutes.

Add the okra and spinach with the lemon juice, and simmer 45-50 minutes, until the greens are completely soft and the stew has genuinely thickened - real molohiya depends on this long, patient simmer.

name: Turkish Cypriot Sheftalia
description: Sheftalia, a beloved island-wide sausage shared across both Turkish and Greek Cypriot cooking, is traditionally wrapped in real caul fat rather than a standard casing, which isn't a practical ingredient here - real technique shapes the seasoned meat into small ovals instead, missing the caul fat's real self-basting effect as it grills.

ingredients.note: tbsp, chopped, standing in for parsley

steps_detailed: Mix the beef with the onion, cilantro, cinnamon, and pepper, kneading well.
Shape into small ovals.
Grill over medium-high heat, turning, 8-10 minutes, until well charred and cooked through.

name: Turkish Cypriot Şiş Kebab
description: Şiş kebab, marinated cubes of meat grilled on skewers, real technique marinating overnight so the flavors genuinely penetrate the meat.
steps_detailed: Marinate the beef in the lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, and oregano for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight.
Thread onto skewers.
Grill over medium-high heat, turning, 10-12 minutes, until charred and cooked through.

name: Turkish Cypriot Halloumi
description: Grilled halloumi, real technique cooking it hot and fast so it chars outside while holding its shape inside, since real halloumi's high melting point keeps it from melting like most cheese.
steps_detailed: Grill or pan-fry the halloumi with no added oil, 2-3 minutes per side, until charred outside and slightly softened within.
Squeeze the lemon juice over and sprinkle with oregano.
Serve immediately while hot.

name: Turkish Cypriot Rice Pilaf
description: Turkish rice, a fragrant pilaf, is a real traditional accompaniment to molohiya and grilled meats across Turkish Cypriot cooking.
steps_detailed: Toast the rice in the butter, 1-2 minutes.
Add the broth, cover, and simmer 15-18 minutes until tender.

name: Turkish Cypriot Yogurt with Radish
description: Yogurt served with fresh radish, real technique keeping this genuinely simple, is a common accompaniment to molohiya across Turkish Cypriot households.
steps_detailed: Serve the yogurt alongside the sliced radish.

name: Turkish Cypriot Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with garlic and lemon, reflecting Turkish Cyprus's rich Mediterranean coastal fishing tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the garlic and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

description: A simple roasted almond snack, common across Turkish Cyprus.
steps_detailed: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 4-5 minutes, until fragrant.
